fields.title: Uterine fibroids
fields.bodyHtml:
Uterine fibroids: advanced treatment in Israel

Uterine fibroids are benign tumours of the smooth muscle tissue of the womb, and occur in many women of reproductive age. Advanced methods of diagnosing and treating uterine fibroids are available in Israel, helping to manage symptoms effectively and prevent possible complications.

Diagnosis of uterine fibroids:

  1. Gynaecological examination:
    The doctor may detect enlargement or distortion of the womb on examination.
  2. Ultrasound scan:
    A transvaginal ultrasound is the standard method for imaging fibroids, allowing their size and position to be assessed.
  3. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI):
    Used for a more precise assessment of the size and position of fibroids, particularly when planning surgery.
  4. Hysteroscopy:
    Visual examination of the inner surface of the womb with an optical instrument, which may be needed to assess submucosal fibroids.
  5. Laboratory tests:
    Blood tests may be ordered to assess haemoglobin levels, particularly where there are symptoms of anaemia due to heavy periods.

Treatments for uterine fibroids:

  1. Drug treatment:
    • Hormone therapy: Medicines such as gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists may be used to shrink fibroids and control symptoms.
    • Non-hormonal medicines: Tranexamic acid, for example, to reduce blood loss during periods.
  2. Surgery:
    • Myomectomy: Removal of the fibroids while preserving the womb — the preferred option for women who wish to retain their fertility.
    • Hysterectomy: Removal of the womb, recommended where other treatments are ineffective or where the fibroids have grown very large.
  3. Minimally invasive procedures:
    • Uterine artery embolisation (UAE): A procedure in which the blood supply to the fibroids is blocked by introducing special substances through a catheter, causing the tumours to shrink.
    • MRI-guided ultrasound ablation: The use of high-intensity focused ultrasound to destroy fibroid tissue under MRI control.

Advantages of treatment in Israel:

  • A multidisciplinary approach: Gynaecologists, radiologists and surgeons work together to draw up an individual treatment plan.
  • Advanced medical equipment: The use of the most modern diagnostic and treatment technology.
  • Individual treatment: All procedures and treatment are adapted to the particular needs of each woman, taking account of her age, general health and wish to preserve her fertility.

Treatment of uterine fibroids in Israel aims to relieve symptoms as effectively and safely as possible while preserving the patient's health and quality of life.

fields.title: Kidney stones
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Kidney stone disease, also known as nephrolithiasis or kidney stones, is a common condition of the urinary system characterised by the formation of hard deposits (stones) in the kidneys or urinary tract. These stones can vary in size and may cause painful symptoms, and can lead to complications if they are not detected and treated in good time. This article looks at the methods of diagnosing and treating kidney stone disease, and at the advantages of treating this condition in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis of kidney stone disease usually begins with a discussion of the patient's medical history and symptoms. Further investigations are then carried out to confirm the presence of stones and establish their type, size and position. The main methods of diagnosing kidney stone disease include:

  • Kidney ultrasound: an ultrasound scan of the kidneys is one of the most accessible and safest methods of diagnosing kidney stone disease. Ultrasound allows stones in the kidneys to be visualised and their characteristics assessed.
  • Computed tomography (CT): a CT scan provides more detailed images of the kidneys and urinary tract, which allows the size and position of the stones to be established more precisely.
  • Urography: an X-ray method in which a contrast medium is introduced to visualise the urinary tract and identify stones.
  • Urine test: a urine test can help identify crystals, which are a precursor to the formation of stones.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of kidney stone disease depends on the type and size of the stones, their number and position, and on whether they are causing symptoms or complications. In some cases stones pass out of the body on their own, but in most cases medical intervention is required. The main treatments for kidney stone disease include:

  • Watchful waiting: in some cases small stones may pass out of the body on their own with plenty of fluids and time. Doctors may recommend regular monitoring and urine tests to follow the situation.
  • Drug treatment: doctors may prescribe medicines that help dissolve stones or reduce the formation of new ones.
  • Extracorporeal shock wave lithotripsy (ESWL): a non-invasive treatment in which sound waves are used to break up the stones so that they can pass out in the urine.
  • Surgical removal of stones: where stones are too large or are causing complications, surgery may be required to remove them.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is known for its high level of medical expertise and advanced technology. Treatment of kidney stone disease in Israel offers the following advantages:

  • Experienced specialists: doctors at Israeli medical centres have extensive experience in treating kidney stone disease. They trained at leading medical schools and are highly competent in this field.
  • Innovative treatments: Israeli medical centres use advanced methods of treating kidney stone disease, which delivers the best results and minimises the risk of complications.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel take account of each patient's particular circumstances and draw up an individual treatment plan to achieve the best results.
  • Comfortable stay: Israel offers a high standard of comfort and service for patients coming for treatment of kidney stone disease.

Conclusion

Kidney stone disease is a serious condition that can lead to painful symptoms and complications. Early detection and treatment play an important part in preventing possible complications and restoring patients' health. Treatment in Israel gives patients access to experienced specialists and advanced treatments, which offers the best chance of overcoming kidney stone disease successfully and restoring quality of life. If you suspect you have kidney stone disease or other problems with your kidneys or urinary tract, we recommend consulting a qualified doctor for an accurate diagnosis and to establish the best treatment plan.

fields.title: Male infertility
fields.bodyHtml:
Introduction

Male infertility is one of the main causes of infertility in couples. It is a medical condition in which a man has difficulty conceiving a child with his partner. Male infertility can have various causes, including reduced sperm quality, obstruction of the urogenital tract, or hormonal disorders. This article looks at the methods of diagnosing and treating male infertility, and at the advantages of treating this condition in Israel.

Methods of diagnosis

Diagnosis of male infertility begins with a medical examination of the patient and the taking of a history. The doctor then orders further tests and investigations to identify the causes of the infertility. The main methods of diagnosing male infertility include:

  • Semen analysis: a test of the semen that assesses the number, movement and shape of the sperm. Semen analysis helps establish the quality of the sperm and the possible causes of infertility.
  • Hormone tests: testing hormone levels can help identify hormonal disorders that may be causing male infertility.
  • Scrotal ultrasound: an ultrasound scan of the scrotum allows its structures to be visualised and any abnormalities identified.
  • Testicular biopsy: in some cases the doctor may recommend a testicular biopsy to examine the tissue and identify the causes of infertility.

Methods of treatment

Treatment of male infertility depends on the causes identified and may involve medicines, surgery or other methods. The main treatments for male infertility include:

  • Drug treatment: doctors may prescribe medicines to raise hormone levels or improve sperm quality.
  • Surgery: an operation may be required to correct abnormalities of the urogenital tract or to restore patency.
  • Intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI): a method of assisted fertilisation in which a single sperm is injected directly into the egg.
  • Intracytoplasmic morphologically selected sperm injection (IMSI): a more thorough method of selecting sperm for fertilisation with the aid of a high-magnification microscope.

Advantages of treatment in Israel

Israel is one of the leading countries in the treatment of male infertility, offering patients advanced treatments and a high level of medical expertise. The advantages of treating male infertility in Israel include:

  • Experienced specialists: doctors at Israeli medical centres have many years of experience in diagnosing and treating male infertility. Their knowledge and skills allow them to approach every case effectively and provide high-quality treatment.
  • The use of advanced technology: Israeli medical centres use advanced methods of diagnosing and treating male infertility, which improves the chances of successful treatment and of conceiving a child.
  • An individual approach: doctors in Israel understand that every patient is different, and draw up an individual treatment plan to achieve the best results.
  • High standards of medical care: the medical infrastructure in Israel meets high standards of quality, ensuring a comfortable stay for patients and effective treatment.

Conclusion

Male infertility is a complex condition that can be treated successfully with modern methods and advanced technology. Establishing the causes of male infertility and choosing the best treatment plan are the key steps towards a successful pregnancy. Israel offers patients high-quality medical care, which makes it an attractive place for the treatment of male infertility. If you or your partner are having difficulty conceiving, we recommend consulting qualified specialists in Israel for professional help and support on the way to fulfilling your dream of parenthood.

fields.title: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
fields.bodyHtml:
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma: advanced treatment in Israel

Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is a group of blood cancers affecting the lymphatic system. In Israel, patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma have access to advanced methods of diagnosis and treatment based on the latest scientific research and clinical experience.

Diagnosis of non-Hodgkin lymphoma

  1. Physical examination and history
    Doctors carry out an examination and gather information about the symptoms and the history of the illness.
  2. Laboratory tests
    These include a full blood count and biochemical tests.
  3. Lymph node biopsy
    Obtaining and histologically examining lymph node tissue to confirm the presence of lymphoma.
    (histology brought from elsewhere can also be reviewed)
  4. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)
    Used to assess how far the tumour has spread in the body.
  5. PET-CT
    A method combining positron emission tomography and computed tomography, allowing the activity of the tumour and the presence of metastases to be assessed.
  6. Bone marrow biopsy and aspiration
    Carried out to identify involvement of the bone marrow.

Treatment of non-Hodgkin lymphoma

  1. Chemotherapy
    The main treatment, aimed at destroying the cancer cells in the body.
  2. Radiotherapy
    Used for localised forms of lymphoma, or to shrink tumours before a stem cell transplant.
  3. Biological and targeted therapy: Includes the use of monoclonal antibodies and other medicines directed at specific molecular targets in the cancer cells.
  4. Stem cell transplant
    Used in relapsed or refractory non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
  5. Immunotherapy
    Includes the use of medicines that stimulate the immune system to fight the cancer cells.

Why patients choose Israel

  • A multidisciplinary approach: specialists from various fields of medicine work together to create an individualised treatment plan.
  • Advanced treatments: patients have access to the most modern treatments, including the latest developments in targeted and immune therapy.
  • Highly qualified specialists: Israel is home to leading world experts in haemato-oncology.
  • An individual approach to treatment: every aspect of treatment is planned with the patient's personal needs and preferences and their physical and psychological condition in mind.

Treatment of non-Hodgkin lymphoma in Israel gives patients access to innovative therapies and a high standard of medical care, which makes it possible to achieve the best results and improve quality of life.
